title: Work & colleagues
goal: Make small talk with colleagues, talk about meetings and deadlines, ask your boss for leave, write a polite message or email, get through a job interview — and understand office news in the passive.
intro:
Pashto at work sounds different from Pashto with friends. With colleagues your own age you'll chat in the easy ته-style you already know; with the boss, clients and interviewers you switch to the **formal register** — تاسو and plural verbs, titles like **مدير صاحب**, formal words like **له … څخه** and **په … اړه**, and set openings for messages: **محترم رئيس صاحب، السلام عليکم**.

Offices and the news also love the **passive**: 'the meeting **was postponed**', 'a decision **was made**', 'you **have been hired**'. Pashto builds it with کېدل, and once you see the pattern you'll hear it everywhere. Expect plenty of English too — *meeting, report, email, project* — wrapped in Pashto grammar.

grammar.title: The formal register: talking to the boss, writing to an office
grammar.body:
Pashto has a clear **formal register** for bosses, officials, clients, interviewers, older people you don't know, and anything written. It comes from a handful of habits:

**1. تاسو and plural verbs, even to one person**: تاسو چېرته **ځئ**؟ · **راشئ** · **کېنئ** · کولای **شئ** چې …؟ To a colleague-friend the same is ته چېرته ځې؟ · راشه · کېنه.

**2. Plural for respect.** Someone you respect is also *talked about* in the plural: مدير صاحب نن نه **دي** راغلي 'the manager hasn't come in today' (lit. have not come, plural). Compare زما همکار نه **دی** راغلی 'my colleague hasn't come in'.

**3. Titles.** **صاحب** after a job title or surname (مدير صاحب، رئيس صاحب، احمدي صاحب، ډاکټر صاحب); **ښاغلی / مېرمن** before a name; **محترم** (to a man) / **محترمې** (to a woman) to open a letter or email.

**4. Formal words.** **له … څخه** 'from' for له … نه · **لطفاً** for مهرباني وکړه · **په … اړه** 'about' · **هيله کوم چې …** 'I kindly ask that …'.

**5. Set openings and closings.** محترم رئيس صاحب، السلام عليکم. … ستاسو له همکارۍ څخه مننه. **په درناوي**، (with respect) + your name.

**The trap** is mixing the two: a title with a ته-verb (مدير صاحب، راشه) sounds rude or comic — say مدير صاحب، **راشئ**.

grammar.title: The passive: 'it was decided', 'I was hired'
grammar.body:
Offices, official letters and the news love the **passive** — the action matters, not who did it. Pashto makes it with **کېدل** 'to become' (perfective **شو**).

**Compound verbs** (adjective or noun + کول) simply swap **کول → کېدل**:
کار مې بشپړ **کړ** 'I finished the work' → کار بشپړ **شو** 'the work was finished'
غونډه يې وروسته **کړه** 'they postponed the meeting' → غونډه وروسته **شوه** 'the meeting was postponed'
پرېکړه **وشوه** 'a decision was made' (from پرېکړه کول).

**Simple verbs** use the **infinitive** + **کېدل**: ليکل **کېږي** 'is (being) written' · **وليکل شو** 'was written' · **ولېږل شو** 'was sent' · **ومنل شو** 'was accepted' · **وګمارل شو** 'was hired'. The perfective و- goes on the infinitive.

**Agreement**: the کېدل part agrees with the **thing or person it happened to**: راپور ولېږل **شو** (m) · غوښتنه ومنل **شوه** (f) · زه وګمارل **شوم** 'I was hired'. Present perfect: غونډه ټاکل **شوې ده** 'the meeting has been set'.

**Impersonal 'it is said'**: **ويل کېږي چې …** (formal, on the news); in everyday talk just **وايي چې …** 'they say …'. In conversation people often prefer an active 'they': هغوی پرېکړه وکړه.

culture:
Arriving at work, you greet everyone — often going round the room to shake hands with each man (women colleagues are usually greeted with a nod and a hand on the heart) — and **ستړي مه شئ** is the perfect office greeting: 'may you not be tired'. Tea comes round all day, and small talk about family (کورنۍ مو ښه ده؟) comes before business.

Use **تاسو** and a title with anyone senior, in any meeting, and in every written message; colleagues your own age slide into ته quickly, but switch back when the boss is in the room. WhatsApp is the real office channel: a message to your boss still starts with سلام + title (سلام مدير صاحب) and ends with مننه or په درناوي.

Kabul NGO offices mix in English (*meeting, report, deadline, email, project*) and Dari; Peshawar offices mix in Urdu and English (*تنخوا* for salary, *چُھټي* for leave). Family events — a wedding, a death, a relative in hospital — are fully accepted reasons for leave, and **يو شخصي کار لرم** 'I have a personal matter' is the polite reason that needs no explanation. In an interview, dress formally, greet with السلام عليکم, use صاحب, and don't call the interviewer by their first name.

lessons.title: Talking to the boss

tip.title: Formal register: تاسو، صاحب، plural verbs
tip.body:
- To the boss, clients, interviewers: **تاسو** + plural verbs even to one person: کېنئ، راشئ، کوئ.
- Add **صاحب** after the title: مدير صاحب، رئيس صاحب.
- Talk *about* a respected person in the plural: مدير صاحب نه **دي** راغلي.
- Never mix a title with a ته-verb.

lessons.title: Meetings and deadlines

tip.title: By when? تر … پورې
tip.body:
- **تر … پورې** = 'by, until': تر جمعې پورې 'by Friday', تر ماښام پورې 'by this evening'.
- The noun after تر goes into the oblique: جمعه → **جمعې**.
- Ask: **تر کله پورې پکار دی؟** 'when is it needed by?'
- Promise with به + perfective: تر سبا پورې به يې **بشپړ کړم**.

lessons.title: Office news: what was decided

tip.title: The passive: وشوه، ولېږل شو
tip.body:
- Compounds swap **کول → کېدل**: بشپړ کړ → بشپړ **شو** 'was finished'; پرېکړه **وشوه** 'it was decided'.
- Simple verbs: infinitive + شو: **ولېږل شو** 'was sent', **ومنل شو** 'was accepted'.
- شو agrees with the thing: راپور ولېږل **شو** (m), غونډه وروسته **شوه** (f).

lessons.title: Asking for time off

tip.title: Asking the boss
tip.body:
- Title first, then a soft question: **مدير صاحب، کولای شم چې …؟** or **اجازه ده چې …؟**
- Or state it politely: **يوه ورځ رخصتي غواړم**.
- Give a reason: a family wedding, illness, or simply **يو شخصي کار لرم**.
- Late? **بښنه غواړم، لږ ځنډ مې وشو.**

sentences.en: Sir, could I take tomorrow off?

sentences.native: زما د تره زوی واده کوي، دوه ورځې رخصتي غواړم.
sentences.roman: zmā də trə zoy wādə́ kawí, dwa wradzé ruxsatí ġwā́ṛəm.
sentences.en: My cousin's getting married — I'd like two days off.

sentences.native: بښنه غواړم، نن ناروغ يم، دفتر ته نه شم راتلای.
sentences.roman: baṣə́na ġwā́ṛəm, nən nāróġ yəm, daftár ta na shəm rātlā́y.
sentences.en: Sorry, I'm ill today and can't come in.

sentences.native: د رخصتۍ غوښتنه مې مدير ته ورکړه.
sentences.roman: də ruxsatə́y ġuṣtə́na me mudír ta wárkṛa.
sentences.en: I gave my leave request to the manager.

sentences.native: ستاسو غوښتنه ومنل شوه.
sentences.roman: stāso ġuṣtə́na wə́manəl shwa.
sentences.en: Your request has been approved.

sentences.native: شخصي کار مې دی، يو ساعت وروسته راځم.
sentences.roman: shaxsí kār me day, yaw sāʿát wrústa rā́dzəm.
sentences.en: I've got a personal errand, I'll be in an hour later.

sentences.native: سړک بند و، ځکه مې ځنډ وشو.
sentences.roman: saṛák band wə, dzə́ka me dzanḍ wə́shu.
sentences.en: The road was closed, that's why I'm late.

sentences.native: مدير صاحب، اجازه ده چې نن لږ وختي لاړ شم؟
sentences.roman: mudír sāhíb, ijāzá da che nən ləẓ waxtí lāṛ shəm?
sentences.en: Sir, may I leave a little early today?

sentences.native: دا زما شخصي خبره ده.
sentences.roman: dā zmā shaxsí xabə́ra da.
sentences.en: That's a private matter.

tip.title: Writing formally
tip.body:
- Open: **محترم** (to a man) / **محترمې** (to a woman) + title + صاحب، السلام عليکم.
- Use formal words: **له … څخه** 'from', **په … اړه** 'about', **هيله کوم چې** 'I kindly ask that'.
- Close: **ستاسو له همکارۍ څخه مننه. په درناوي،** + your name.
- Always تاسو, never ته.

sentences.native: محترم مدير صاحب، راپور مې تاسو ته ولېږه.
sentences.roman: muhtarám mudír sāhíb, rāpór me tāso ta wə́leẓə.
sentences.en: Dear Manager, I've sent you the report.

sentences.native: محترمې مېرمن احمدي، السلام عليکم.
sentences.roman: muhtaráme mermə́n ahmadí, assalā́mu ʿaláykum.
sentences.en: Dear Mrs Ahmadi, (greetings).

sentences.native: له تاسو څخه هيله کوم چې ما ته ځواب راکړئ.
sentences.roman: la tāso tsəxa híla kawə́m che mā ta dzawā́b rā́kṛəy.
sentences.en: I would kindly ask you to reply to me.

sentences.native: زما ايميل مو وليد؟
sentences.roman: zmā imél mo wə́lid?
sentences.en: Did you see my email? (polite)

sentences.native: د رسمي رخصتۍ په اړه يو ايميل راغی.
sentences.roman: də rasmí ruxsatə́y pə aṛá yaw imél rā́ġay.
sentences.en: An email came round about the public holiday.

sentences.native: د ټولو همکارانو له همکارۍ څخه مننه.
sentences.roman: də ṭolo hamkārā́no la hamkārə́y tsəxa manə́na.
sentences.en: Thank you to all colleagues for your cooperation.

sentences.native: په درناوي، فريد.
sentences.roman: pə dranāwí, faríd.
sentences.en: Respectfully, Farid. (closing a message)

sentences.native: په رسمي ايميل کې ته مه ليکئ، تاسو وليکئ.
sentences.roman: pə rasmí imél ke tə ma líkəy, tāso wə́likəy.
sentences.en: In a formal email, don't write ته — write تاسو.

sentences.native: رئيس صاحب، که اجازه وي، سبا له کوره کار وکړم؟
sentences.roman: raʾís sāhíb, ka ijāzá wi, sabā́ la kóra kār wə́kṛəm?
sentences.en: Sir, if it's all right with you, may I work from home tomorrow?

sentences.native: ستاسو ايميل ته به ژر ځواب درکړم.
sentences.roman: stāso imél ta ba zhər dzawā́b dárkṛəm.
sentences.en: I'll reply to your email soon.

lessons.title: A job interview
new: ستاسو د دندې مرکه سبا لس بجې ده.

sentences.native: سبا مې د دندې مرکه ده، ډېر پرېشان يم.
sentences.roman: sabā́ me də dánde markə́ da, ḍer pareshā́n yəm.
sentences.en: I've got a job interview tomorrow, I'm really nervous.

sentences.native: مرکې ته رسمي جامې واغونده.
sentences.roman: marké ta rasmí jā́me wā́ġunda.
sentences.en: Wear formal clothes to the interview.

sentences.native: ستاسو تجربه څو کاله ده؟
sentences.roman: stāso tajrubá tso kā́la da?
sentences.en: How many years of experience do you have?

sentences.native: ما په يوه اداره کې درې کاله کار کړی دی.
sentences.roman: mā pə yáwa idārá ke dre kā́la kār kaṛay day.
sentences.en: I've worked at an organisation for three years.

sentences.native: ولې مو له تېرې دندې استعفا ورکړه؟
sentences.roman: wə́le mo la tére dánde istiʿfā́ wárkṛa?
sentences.en: Why did you resign from your last job?

sentences.native: زه وګمارل شوم! سبا کار شروع کوم.
sentences.roman: zə wə́gumārəl shwəm! sabā́ kār shurúʿ kawə́m.
sentences.en: I got the job! I start tomorrow.

sentences.native: هغه زموږ نوی مدير وګمارل شو.
sentences.roman: haġá zmuẓ náway mudír wə́gumārəl shu.
sentences.en: He has been appointed our new manager.

sentences.native: معاش به څومره وي؟
sentences.roman: maʿā́sh ba tsómra wi?
sentences.en: What would the salary be?

sentences.native: له کومې ورځې کار شروع کړم؟
sentences.roman: la kúme wradzé kār shurúʿ kṛəm?
sentences.en: From which day should I start?

sentences.native: ستاسو د ځواب انتظار به کوم.
sentences.roman: stāso də dzawā́b intizā́r ba kawə́m.
sentences.en: I'll look forward to hearing from you.
